data.content_ref: inline:Replace the primitive acceptance test with a derived, polynomial-time skeptical-defeat pre-order over attackers: a node is accepted iff no attacker strictly precedes it in the pre-order and is itself undefeated. On well-founded graphs this coincides with the grounded extension; on cyclic graphs it extends it while preserving determinism and polynomial cost, at the price of reinstatement becoming primitive rather than derived. This is criticizable for potentially breaking the committed-root validity guarantee on mixed cyclic/acyclic graphs, and for requiring a new proof that the pre-order is well-defined and consistent across the fixpoint.
